messages:
Alex Chen: Heads up — customer acme-corp on Dedicated pool d-51 reporting surge of 503s and sustained tail latency since 09:12 UTC. They saw large numbers of long-context (>32k) requests and sudden throttle spikes. Error: "model_request_throttled". 

Maria Gonzalez: Can you paste a sample request id and tenant id? Also which model variant? Might be KV cache churn from long prefixes.

Alex Chen: tenant: acme-tenant-7, req id: 01FQZ4R9, model: redwood-13b-16k-q4. Logs show repeated "cache_evict" events and "kv_fragmentation" warnings. Pasting excerpt:
```
[09:12:15] evict_count=1423 tenant=acme-tenant-7 worker=rt-12
[09:12:15] kv_frag_percent=48.2 tenant=acme-tenant-7
[09:12:16] serve_err=throttle model=redwood-13b-16k-quant msg="no available kv slots"
```

Jess (support): Repro steps requested by SRE: 1) use long-prefix prompt (~30k tokens) hitting same model on Dedicated pool, 2) hammer at 10rps from 3 clients for 2 minutes, 3) observe evictions and 503s. Can someone run a quick repro? I'll coordinate with the customer.

OpsBot: [alert] DedicatedPool d-51 - prefix_kv_pressure high for tenant acme-tenant-7 (90th=71ms, evict_rate spike)

Infra Oncall: Confirming autoscaler didn't immediately scale. It logged backoff due to "min_capacity_reached" and we also hit per-tenant KV quota. Seems autoscaler waited 45s before provisioning new workers.

Samir Patel: That 45s backoff combined with aggressive KV eviction can cause cascading throttles. Two possible mitigations: 1) temporary tenant QoS flag to throttle long-context requests for acme-tenant-7, 2) bump dedicated pool by +2 workers or enable burst capacity. Recommend applying 1) first to stop further churn.

Maria Gonzalez: Can we get a quick patch to TTL for KV entries from 10m -> 3m for that tenant? That would free slots faster but risks cold tokens. Also reduce per-request max_prefix_tokens to 24k for their tenant.

Infra Oncall: I can flip tenant QoS and lower prefix_tokens cap. Applying change now: `PATCH /internal/tenants/acme-tenant-7/qos {"max_prefix_tokens":24000,"kv_ttl_sec":180}`

Alex Chen: After the QoS change latency dropped and evict_count decreased in metrics within 30s. Customer still seeing some 503s but much less. Will continue monitoring. 

Jess (support): I've opened escalation ticket RWD-INC-8934 and notified account team. Customer asked for RCA and timeline.

Samir Patel: Root cause hypothesis: noisy long-context workload caused high fragmentation of the per-tenant KV arena; combined with autoscaler backoff and per-tenant slot limits caused transient capacity exhaustion and throttling. Mitigations: tenant caps, aggressive TTLs, faster autoscale policy (reduce backoff), and a reclaim task to defragment KV arenas. I'll draft a runbook.

Infra Oncall: Adding next steps — schedule a hotfix change to autoscaler backoff (reduce initial backoff to 5s for dedicated pools under pressure), and create a task to add compaction pass on idle workers. 

Alex Chen: Thanks all. I'll share logs and a short repro script with the ticket. For the customer: ask them to retry with smaller prefixes or fall back to the 8k model variant while we stabilize.

Jess (support): Noted. Closing loop with acme-corp and will share RCA when ready. :thumbsup:
